title: Setting Up ImGui with Win32 and DirectX 11
summary: Dear ImGui is a handful of source files you add to your project, plus a **platform back end** (input and windows) and a **renderer back end** (drawing). This lesson builds the standard Win32 + DirectX 11 program step by step, the same set-up as ImGui's own example.
ideas:
- Build `examples/example_win32_directx11` from the ImGui repository and run it.
- Then create your own empty Win32 project, add the files from the table, and reproduce the example from scratch with the code above.

cards.q: Which files make up a typical Win32 + DirectX 11 ImGui set-up?
cards.a: The ImGui core .cpp and .h files plus imgui_impl_win32 and imgui_impl_dx11 from the backends folder.

cards.q: List the calls at the start and end of every frame.
cards.a: ImGui_ImplDX11_NewFrame, ImGui_ImplWin32_NewFrame, ImGui::NewFrame at the start; ImGui::Render and ImGui_ImplDX11_RenderDrawData(ImGui::GetDrawData()) at the end.

cards.q: In what order do you shut ImGui down?
cards.a: The renderer back end, the platform back end, then DestroyContext: the reverse of setting up.
